about.title: Patterson Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Patterson's economy runs on distribution centers, agriculture, and the trucking that moves through corridors like Sperry Avenue and Las Palmas Avenue, and workplace injuries here often happen in warehouses, on delivery routes, or at farm operations near town. In California, workers' compensation is generally the exclusive remedy against your employer, meaning you typically can't sue them directly even if they were careless. But that's not the whole story — if a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate third-party claim outside the workers' comp system. That distinction matters, especially for injuries involving forklifts, delivery trucks, or machinery from outside vendors. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle claims directly. We're a free service that connects injured workers in Patterson with an independent attorney who can look at the facts of your situation and explain what options, if any, might apply.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Workplace Injury

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Picture
items.desc: While workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — may still be liable for a separate injury claim.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Are Short
items.desc: California generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, so waiting too long can complicate your ability to get benefits started.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, But Workers Still Worry
items.desc: It's against California law for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim, and an attorney can help you understand your protections.

items.question: I was hurt while making a delivery near Rt 33 in Patterson — can I file a claim against my employer?
items.answer: In most cases, California workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer, so a direct lawsuit typically isn't available regardless of fault. However, if another driver or a third party contributed to the crash, you may have a separate claim against them. An independent attorney can review the details and explain what applies to your specific situation.

items.question: What if my injury involved equipment from an outside company?
items.answer: If a piece of machinery, a delivery vehicle, or equipment from a vendor or manufacturer played a role in your injury, that may open the door to a third-party claim outside the workers' comp system. These claims generally carry a two-year deadline in California, so it helps to have someone look at the facts sooner rather than later.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a workplace injury in Patterson?
items.answer: No — California law prohibits retaliation against workers for reporting an injury or filing a workers' comp claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, it's worth discussing with an independent attorney who can explain your options given the specifics of your case.
